_comment: AN-FORECAST (R340, R281). THE ONE FORECAST CONTRACT, bound on both sides.
A weekly rhythm plus a fixed 'today' go in; the imagined working days to 31 December come out,
and the recorded days plus those imagined days, run through the SHARED aggregation (toTeleworkInput)
and the engine (calculateTelework), produce the projection rate. The Kotlin side reads this file
through ch.monreleve.app.dossier.imaginedEntriesToYearEnd + toTeleworkInput + calculateTelework;
the web side (FW-FORECAST) reads the SAME file through its own date function and engine. A one-digit
change here fails BOTH suites (the plant, verified and reverted, is recorded in REPORT-AN-FORECAST.txt).
R340: A PROJECTION IS NEVER A RECORD. These rows are computed in memory and nothing here is ever
written to the entries, the mutation queue, the server, the releve, the PDF or the annex.
rhythm: Monday..Friday, each assigned the kind worked that weekday (HOME = Domicile / teletravail,
CH = Suisse). A weekday the rhythm leaves OUT is not a worked day and is imagined as nothing. The
kinds use the engine's EntryKind names so both languages speak one vocabulary.
today: the day the projection is requested (a fixed clock in the test). The imagined set is every
working day STRICTLY AFTER today to 31 December; today itself is never imagined (it is recorded or
it is not). Public holidays and leave are NOT deducted - on the 240-day basis that overstates
telework, so the projection warns early, never late (the screen says so).
recorded: the days already recorded by 'today' (the full row shape, as aggregation-cases.json).
expected.imaginedWorkingDays: all imagined rows (HOME + CH weekdays in range).
expected.imaginedTeleworkDays: the HOME rows among them.
expected.currentRate: the engine's declarableRate on the RECORDED days alone (today's figure).
expected.declarableRate: the engine's declarableRate on recorded + imagined (the December projection).
Both rates are the AFC declarable rate (truncated to two decimals), a percentage. Every case here is
under 40% at GE / 100% / simplified240, so declarableRate = truncate(teleworkDays / 240 x 100, 2).

cases.note: The design's own example: Domicile Tuesday+Thursday, Suisse otherwise, requested 9 October 2026. 59 jours ouvres remain, 24 of them Tuesdays/Thursdays. No days recorded here, so the projection is 24 telework / 240.
All five weekdays Domicile, requested 24 December 2026 (a Thursday). Five weekdays remain (Fri 25, Mon 28, Tue 29, Wed 30, Thu 31) - holidays not deducted - all telework.
Three days already recorded at Domicile plus five imagined Domicile days: the projection combines record and rhythm. 3/240 today becomes 8/240 by December.

Ten days recorded at Domicile, a rhythm of five Suisse days: the imagined CH days are worked days (counted in imaginedWorkingDays) but add no telework, so the projection equals today's figure. Proves a Suisse rhythm does not move the rate.
A partial rhythm (only Tuesday and Thursday set, the other weekdays left out) requested 24 December 2026: only the Tuesday (29) and Thursday (31) are imagined - two working days, both telework.
